article.name: archeus
article.summary: Archeus is a local workspace and memory layer for coding agents. It builds a per-project semantic graph from repository files and session transcripts, then exposes compact project memory through a launcher digest, path-scoped rules, and optional prompt-time retrieval. A separate lesson pipeline extracts durable decisions and corrections from sessions.

contact.note: Checked the official README.md and SECURITY.md at the reviewed revision; neither publishes a contact email. The SECURITY.md directs vulnerability reports to GitHub private vulnerability reporting.

who_what.text: The public repository and README describe Archeus as a local memory and workspace layer for AI coding agents, built by Babar Muhammad Anas and licensed MIT. The inspected project-memory feature is part of the larger Python application, with a terminal UI, desktop GUI, and Claude Code plugin surfaces; the README also describes Codex and pi compatibility.

architecture.text: Code observation: `claude_sessions.memory` stores a versioned JSON graph under the project work directory's `.archeus/memory/graph.json` and mirrors it under Archeus's encoded project folder when available. The graph holds entities, relations, repo/module summaries, source provenance, module dependency edges, refresh state, conflicts, stale counts, and aggregate model-call cost fields. Writes use the project's atomic JSON helper; a shrink can record a graph snapshot before saving.

Code and documentation observation: background refresh extracts codebase and module information with a headless model call, incrementally using file state/content hashes, then merges this with dependency information. Source constants bound per-file and per-batch input and per-module representative files. A per-project exclusive scan lock coordinates refreshes; the documentation describes capped background cycles, queued work, progress, and saving progress between steps.

The guide describes three context surfaces: a small always-on CLAUDE.md micro-index, lazy per-module `.claude/rules/` files, and an optional UserPromptSubmit hook that retrieves a task-related subgraph. The recall engine is local lexical ranking; it does not call a model to rank each prompt. A separate project `worklog` can contribute a small number of recent session episodes.

behavior.text: Write/build — a project memory build scans source files and sends bounded module content to the configured headless model for entities and relations; it also incorporates dependency edges and repo/module summaries. Refresh is incremental. The inspected interface is build/refresh-oriented; no general per-fact user-authored CRUD API was established in the reviewed memory and recall files.

Update — when a refresh no longer supports an existing fact, the implementation can mark it invalid and timestamp invalidation rather than immediately removing it. Recall excludes invalid entities. The source defines a bounded invalidated-history count and age window; entity loss can be snapshotted before graph save, with the documentation describing a 12-version history.

Delete/forget — the inspected memory model includes eviction and graph-shrinking paths, and the documentation describes pruning with preview/confirmation and undo through snapshots. I did not establish a universal per-entity hard-delete API, nor physical erasure behavior for snapshots, sidecars, backups, or mirrored copies from the bounded files inspected.

Retrieval — recall builds a local index over names and summaries, uses lexical overlap, path/module matches, dependency rank and lesson confidence, combines rankings with reciprocal-rank fusion, and expands selected entities through relations. Invalid facts and pending lessons are skipped. The renderer adds only items that fit the remaining token budget instead of truncating a long item; it returns an empty result for a blank query or empty graph.

Lesson write/review — after sessions, lesson extraction asks the configured model for a bounded set of durable error/fix pairs, decisions, corrections and preferences from transcript tails. Lessons carry kind and confidence; people can approve, pin or evict them. The recall path only injects approved or pinned lessons, while configured confidence auto-approval is described in the project guide.

Scope — the graph is selected by project path and encoded project folder, so normal code memory is project-oriented. Lesson scans include sessions for the same project across accounts, and convention processing intentionally scans project graphs across accounts; qualifying preferences, corrections or decisions may be promoted into a user-level CLAUDE.md shared across projects. This global convention surface is a deliberate scope expansion.

Provenance/evidence — graph provenance and module refresh state track the source files/modules processed; session lessons originate from transcript sessions. Returned memory text includes entity names, summaries, and associated files where available. The inspected graph schema does not provide claim-level citations to source passages or an external evidence adjudication protocol, so source lineage does not prove factual support.

Source-visible efficiency and observability — code sets input bounds, an entity cap, invalid-history limits, query budgets, and scan locks; the docs describe the always-on and per-prompt token budgets. Recall appends only actually injected item names to a hits sidecar, and a later graph build folds those hits into reinforcement; preview mode does not log hits. Graph state includes cumulative cost fields, and UI/docs expose refresh status and spend. These are mechanisms and source-reported limits, not benchmark measurements.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval and abstention are unmeasured. Lexical overlap, stopword handling, and empty-query behavior are code observations; no answerability or unanswerable-query evaluation was run.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate are unmeasured. Superseding a fact can invalidate it and preserve bounded history; no correction probes or stale-answer adjudication were run.
Deletion leakage is unmeasured. Eviction, invalidation, snapshots and multiple graph locations are visible; no deleted-fact retrieval or physical-erasure checks were performed.

Scope-isolation leakage is unmeasured. Ordinary project graphs are project-oriented, while lesson mining spans accounts for that project and convention promotion is cross-project/user-level by design; no isolation workload was run.

Evidence support precision and citation coverage are unmeasured. The review found source-file/module lineage and transcript origins, but no required claim-level source citations; no claim support adjudication was performed.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay are unmeasured. Documentation gives target/source-described local behavior, but no runtime timings were collected for this review.
Tokens, model cost and storage efficiency are unmeasured. Source contains token budget controls and aggregate cost fields, but no token/cost/storage observations were recorded for this system.
The shared benchmark record is `not_run`; fixture probe counts describe a planned workload and are not results for Archeus.

limits: This is a bounded source review of the pinned README, project-memory guide, memory/recall/lesson/convention code, and security policy; it does not establish runtime behavior or cover every UI, plugin, storage, and session subsystem.
No system process, benchmark, or tests were run. Retrieval quality, abstention, latency, refresh delay, cost, storage growth, and concurrent-workload behavior remain unmeasured.

The inspected graph has source/module lineage but no claim-level citations; the review cannot establish that extracted facts are correct or that a retrieved summary is supported by the referenced source.
Physical deletion across snapshots, mirrored graphs, sidecars, transcripts, and backups was not established. Cross-project conventions deliberately broaden the audience of some lesson content.

benchmark.note: The project execution record is not_run and contains no Archeus measurements. The fixture is a planned workload only. This review did not execute Archeus, benchmarks, or tests.
